subject: Mathematics
title: Indefinite Integrals
summary: Integration is the reverse of differentiation (antiderivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions): ∫f(x)dx = F(x) + C where F′(x) = f(x). Every answer can be checked by differentiating.
Main methods: standard formulas, substitution, integration by parts (ILATE), partial fractions and special standard forms (1/(x² ± a²), √(a² − x²) etc.).
JEE shortcuts: ∫eˣ(f + f′)dx = eˣf + C, and integrals of the form ∫f′(x)/f(x) dx = ln|f(x)| + C.

formulas.name: Trigonometric integrals
formulas.formula: ∫sin x = −cos x;  ∫cos x = sin x;  ∫sec²x = tan x;  ∫tan x = ln|sec x|;  ∫sec x = ln|sec x + tan x|;  ∫cosec x = ln|cosec x − cot x|

formulas.name: Standard forms I
formulas.formula: ∫dx/(x² + a²) = (1/a)tan⁻¹(x/a);  ∫dx/(x² − a²) = (1/2a)ln|(x − a)/(x + a)|;  ∫dx/(a² − x²) = (1/2a)ln|(a + x)/(a − x)|

formulas.name: Substitution
formulas.when: Spotting an inner function and its derivative.

formulas.name: Integration by parts
formulas.formula: ∫u v dx = u∫v dx − ∫(u′∫v dx)dx;  choose u by ILATE (Inverse trig, Log, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential)

formulas.name: eˣ shortcut
formulas.when: Integrals with eˣ times a function plus its derivative.

formulas.name: Partial fractions
formulas.formula: (px + q)/((x − a)(x − b)) = A/(x − a) + B/(x − b);  repeated factor (x − a)²: A/(x − a) + B/(x − a)²;  quadratic factor: (Bx + C)/(x² + bx + c)
formulas.note: If degree of numerator ≥ denominator, divide first.

formulas.name: Linear over quadratic
formulas.formula: ∫(px + q)/(ax² + bx + c)dx: write px + q = A(2ax + b) + B, then split

formulas.name: Trig powers
formulas.formula: sin²x = (1 − cos 2x)/2;  cos²x = (1 + cos 2x)/2;  odd power: save one factor and substitute

formulas.name: a sin x + b cos x forms
formulas.formula: ∫dx/(a + b cos x): use t = tan(x/2), cos x = (1 − t²)/(1 + t²), dx = 2dt/(1 + t²)

examples.title: By parts
examples.solution: u = x, v = eˣ: x eˣ − ∫eˣ dx = (x − 1)eˣ + C.

examples.title: Log integral
examples.solution: By parts with u = ln x, v = 1: x ln x − x + C.

examples.title: eˣ shortcut
examples.solution: f = sin x, f′ = cos x ⇒ eˣ sin x + C.

topics.title: Checking answers
topics.explain: Differentiate the result; you should get the integrand back. Constants of integration can make two correct answers look different (e.g. sin²x vs −cos²x/2 forms).

topics.title: Choosing a substitution
topics.explain: Look for a function and its derivative: ∫2x/(x² + 1)dx → t = x² + 1 gives ln(x² + 1). For √(ax + b), put t² = ax + b.

topics.title: Trig substitutions
topics.explain: √(a² − x²): x = a sin θ;  √(a² + x²): x = a tan θ;  √(x² − a²): x = a sec θ.

topics.title: Integrals of rational functions of sin and cos
topics.explain: Divide numerator and denominator by cos²x to get sec²x dx and substitute t = tan x, especially for ∫dx/(a sin²x + b cos²x).

topics.title: Reduction formulas
topics.explain: ∫sinⁿx dx = −sinⁿ⁻¹x cos x/n + ((n − 1)/n)∫sinⁿ⁻²x dx — leads to Wallis' formula for definite integrals.

topics.title: Special trick for ∫(x² + 1)/(x⁴ + 1)
topics.explain: Divide by x²: ∫(1 + 1/x²)/(x² + 1/x²) dx, then put t = x − 1/x. For (x² − 1)/(x⁴ + 1) use t = x + 1/x.

ratta: ∫tan x = ln|sec x|;  ∫sec x = ln|sec x + tan x|.
ILATE for u in by parts.
